name: Taranis

attributes.attribute: linked by the Romans to Jupiter
honored by a sacrifice burned alive

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Taranis is a mainland Celtic god. He rules thunder and the fire that follows. His name comes from a Celtic word for thunder. He is shown with a hammer. The Romans held Taranis to be the chief god of the Celts and linked him to Jupiter. The poet Lucan wrote that his rite asked for a live offering that was burned. Taranis was not the head of a company of gods.

okr.objective: Describe Taranis, the mainland Celtic thunder god.
key_results: Taranis rules thunder and the fire that follows.
The Romans linked Taranis to their god Jupiter.
His rite used human sacrifice, the victims burned alive.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
